turns.en: Sweet. Okay. I'll take us to another recurring corner in the podcast, Contrarian Corner. What's something that you believe that a lot of other people don't believe? What's kind of a contrarian take about anything that comes to mind?
turns.zh: 不错。好的，我要带大家进入播客的另一个固定环节——“反向思考角”。你认为有多少人不认同的观点是什么？关于人工智能（AI）或其他任何话题，你有什么不同见解？

turns.speaker: Evan Spiegel
turns.en: Well, I think for me, we're in an industry where so much of the conversation is focused on technology. And I think maybe my contrarian point of view or my contrarian angle is humanity is far more important than the technological developments, largely because humanity dictates how technology is adopted. I think for example, right now, people are massively underestimating the role that human adoption and human comfort with advances in artificial intelligence will determine its deployment. I think technology leaders think that folks will just blindly adopt new technology as it comes out. (01:04:52): And I think we're going to enter a period of time where there's going to be a huge amount of societal pushback on a lot of the changes that are coming with AI. And so I think a lot of our focus as an industry, but more broadly in the world needs to be putting humanity first, making sure that the tools we're developing are advancing humanity's goals in addition to business goals. And I think in our industry at least, that's a bit contrarian.
turns.zh: 嗯，我觉得在我们这个行业里，大家讨论最多的都是技术方面的话题。而我个人的反向观点或视角是，人类远比技术发展更为重要，主要是因为人类决定了技术的应用方式。比如说，现在人们严重低估了人工智能（AI）在人类采用和适应过程中所起的作用。很多人以为技术领导者认为人们会盲目接受新技术。（01:04:52）但我认为，我们即将迎来一个时期，社会将对人工智能带来的诸多变革产生巨大抵触。因此，我认为我们这个行业乃至整个社会都需要把人放在首位，确保我们开发的工具在服务商业目标的同时，还要助力人类实现更远大的目标。至少在我们这个行业里，这确实有些与众不同。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah. And just so we don't need to go too down this path, but it's so hard for the AI labs, I think, to on the one hand be like, okay, this is really dangerous if it gets much smarter and we need people to know this because this is happening and moving quickly. On the other hand, how do you not just freak everyone out and make everyone so afraid of where things are going? It's like, well, what do you do? What's the right thing for them to do? (01:05:37): And because of all that doom and gloom, I'm sure you've seen these surveys. AI is below ICE in terms of popularity and below Iran. This isn't going great. I don't know. I don't know what I would do if I were the lab. And I love, I guess that's like a benefit of Snapchat is it makes like you guys have been in AI for a very long time and it shows you the playfulness of it all and it doesn't have to be that serious. (01:06:03): Anyway, with that, Evan, we reached our very exciting lightning round. I've got five questions for you. Are you ready?
turns.zh: 是的。不过我们没必要深挖这个话题，但人工智能实验室现在确实面临着巨大挑战。一方面，他们需要告知公众，如果人工智能变得更加智能，可能会带来危险，而公众需要了解这一进程并保持警惕。另一方面，他们又不能让所有人感到恐慌，认为技术发展方向令人担忧。这真是个两难的困境。（01:05:37）正因如此，种种悲观情绪导致相关调查显示，人工智能在公众受欢迎程度上仅次于移民和边境执法局（ICE），甚至低于伊朗。这情况可不妙。我不知道，如果我是实验室负责人，我该怎么做呢？不过说实话，我很庆幸自己在Snapchat上分享过这些经历。这让我意识到，你们这些在人工智能领域深耕多年的老手们，看到技术的趣味性一面是多么重要——它本不必如此严肃。

turns.speaker: Evan Spiegel
turns.en: Let's give it a shot.
turns.zh: 那我们试试看。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay. What are two or three books that you find yourself recommending most to other people?
turns.zh: 好的。你最常向别人推荐的两三本书是什么？

turns.speaker: Evan Spiegel
turns.en: Well, you know what I just finished was The First 50 Years of Apple by David Pogue. I thought it was great. I would recommend the first half because he interviews like 150 early Apple team members and the stories are just great and there's a lot of learnings in there. So I really enjoyed that. I think ... What else have I read recently? There's a great book maybe relevant for this particular moment called The End of the World is just the Beginning, which actually touches a lot on the vulnerability of global shipping. The global economy is built on global shipping, and it sort of predicts a world where the US was going to have a much harder time securing the global waterways. And what does that mean for the way that we build things and organize ourselves as a society?
turns.zh: 嗯，你知道我刚读完的是大卫·波格的《苹果的头五十年》。我觉得很棒。我会推荐前半部分，因为他采访了约150位苹果早期团队成员，那些故事非常精彩，里面有很多值得借鉴的地方。所以我很喜欢这本书。最近我还读了一本与当下形势相关的书，叫《世界末日才刚刚开始》，它着重探讨了全球航运的脆弱性。全球经济建立在全球航运之上，而书中预测了一个美国在保障全球航道方面面临巨大挑战的世界。这对我们构建事物和组织社会的方式意味着什么？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That sounds quite familiar these days.
turns.zh: 这听起来和当下情况很相似。

turns.speaker: Evan Spiegel
turns.en: Quite relevant for the given moment we're at.
turns.zh: 就我们当下所处的这个时刻而言，这确实非常贴切。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. Is there a recent movie or TV show you have really enjoyed?
turns.zh: 太棒了。你最近有没有特别喜欢的电影或电视剧？

turns.speaker: Evan Spiegel
turns.en: I mean, I feel like this is so typical, but I loved Marty Supreme. I thought that movie was off the charts and I was like ... I don't know. I'm not used to watching stuff that extreme. I was on the edge of my seat the whole time. It's like a full throttle movie experience. Highly recommend.
turns.zh: 我是说，我觉得这太常见了，但我超爱《马蒂至尊》。我觉得那部电影简直太棒了，而且我当时就……我也不知道。我不习惯看这么极端的作品。我全程都坐立不安。这真是一次全速前进的观影体验。强烈推荐。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I've not seen it yet. I keep hearing amazing things.
turns.zh: 我还没看过。不过听说评价超高。

turns.speaker: Evan Spiegel
turns.en: It's very intense. Yeah.
turns.zh: 太激烈了。是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.speaker: Evan Spiegel
turns.en: Ready for that.
turns.zh: 准备好了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Next question. Is there a product you recently discovered that you really love? Could be an app, could be clothing, gadget, anything.
turns.zh: 下一个问题。你最近有没有发现特别喜欢的产品？可以是应用、服装、电子产品，什么都行。

turns.speaker: Evan Spiegel
turns.en: Well, I think through our kids right now, I'm just rediscovering Pokemon, which is so fun. It's so great. And I think there's so much art to it and personality and character and what an amazing brand and franchise. And I think my general view is there's just so, so much they could do to grow that IP and franchise, at least if our kids are any indication.
turns.zh: 嗯，我现在通过孩子重新发现了宝可梦，真是太有趣了。太棒了。我觉得它在艺术性、个性和角色塑造方面都下了很多功夫，是个超棒的品牌和IP。至少从我们孩子的反应来看，我觉得这个IP和品牌还有很大的发展空间。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: First mention of Pokemon in the lightning ground. Next question. Do you have a favorite life motto that you often come back to in work or in life?
turns.zh: 这是闪电环节中首次提到宝可梦。下一个问题。你有没有人生格言，工作或生活中经常回味的？

turns.speaker: Evan Spiegel
turns.en: You have two ears and one mouth. Use them in that proportion.
turns.zh: 两只耳朵一张嘴。用起来要保持这个比例。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Nice. Final question. You guys have created many lenses over the years. I'm curious if you have just a favorite lens, like all time favorite and then all time least favorite, the worst.
turns.zh: 不错。最后一个问题。你们这些年开发了很多镜头。我很好奇有没有最喜欢的镜头，比如最喜欢的和最不喜欢的、最糟糕的。

turns.speaker: Evan Spiegel
turns.en: I mean, all time favorite is probably the vomiting rainbow. I think that just brought so much joy to so many people, which is great. Least favorite, probably the old lens, I don't know, or face swap.
turns.zh: 嗯，最喜欢的可能是呕吐彩虹。我觉得它给很多人带来了欢乐，真是太棒了。最不喜欢的可能是老镜头，或者换脸功能。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Oh, right.
turns.zh: 哦，对。

turns.speaker: Evan Spiegel
turns.en: Those are intense. Yeah.
turns.zh: 那些太激烈了。是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow. Flashback. And you guys were the first to do that, right?
turns.zh: 哇。回忆杀。你们可是最先做这个的，对吧？

turns.speaker: Evan Spiegel
turns.en: Yeah. I mean, and that was all early days, real-time machine learning transformation on the device. So that was pretty cutting edge at the time. I mean, I don't think people realize that Bobby created our gen AI lab 10 years ago, a decade ago, or something like that.
turns.zh: 是的。我是说，当时还处于早期阶段，在设备上实时进行机器学习转换。在当时来说，这真的非常前沿。我觉得人们没意识到，十年前，鲍比就创立了我们的通用AI实验室。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What a time, the face swapping era.
turns.zh: 真是段美好的时光，换脸功能的时代。

turns.speaker: Evan Spiegel
turns.en: The early use of generative AI in action.
turns.zh: 早期在实际应用中运用生成式AI。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow. I forgot that was another innovation. And then there's businesses and apps that built that as a whole business and then all went away as far as I can tell. Wow. That was a good time. All right. Well, Evan, is there anything else you wanted to share? Anything else you want to leave listeners with before I let you go?
turns.zh: 哇。我都忘了这也是一项创新。然后有一些企业和应用把它发展成了一整个业务，但后来又都消失了。哇。那真是段美好的时光。好的，埃文，你还有什么想分享的吗？在我结束采访前，你有什么想留给听众的吗？

turns.speaker: Evan Spiegel
turns.en: I think it's such an exciting time. Obviously, I think there's a lot of concern about the way that artificial intelligence is going to change our society, but I think there's so much to be optimistic about in terms of the way that computing can become more human, and that's really what we're focused on. So really excited to share more about all the stuff we've been working on, later this year.
turns.zh: 我觉得这真是个令人兴奋的时代。显然，人们对人工智能将如何改变我们的社会存在诸多担忧，但就计算技术如何变得更具人性化而言，我们有充分的理由保持乐观，而这正是我们目前致力于探索的方向。所以，我非常期待在今年晚些时候向大家深入分享我们一直以来所做的努力。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Evan, thank you so much for being here.
turns.zh: 埃文，非常感谢你能来参加今天的活动。

turns.speaker: Evan Spiegel
turns.en: My pleasure. Thanks, Lenny.
turns.zh: 不客气。谢谢你，莱尼。
